subject: Information Theory
title: Natural Selection as Channel Coding
description: Learn Natural Selection as Channel Coding in one minute.

hook.text: A population is a noisy channel. The environment is the noise. Natural selection decodes the signal of fitness.

buildup.text: Each generation, random mutations add noise to the genome. Selection filters harmful changes and keeps beneficial ones.

discovery.text: Over time, the genome accumulates information about the environment—encoded as adaptations that improve survival.

twist.text: The maximum rate of adaptation is bounded by population size and mutation rate—an evolutionary channel capacity.

climax.text: Fisher's theorem: the rate of fitness increase equals the genetic variance in fitness. More variance, faster learning.

punchline.text: Evolution is learning. The genome is the student.

quiz.question: What does the genome accumulate over evolutionary time?
options: Information about the environment encoded as adaptations
